result:
Compiles cleanly. I've written `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/FractionAgentTest.java` — a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering:

- All 12 documented constant fields (`ZERO`, `ONE`, halves/thirds/quarters/fifths)
- All 5 static factories (`getFraction(double/int,int/int,int,int/String)`, `getReducedFraction`) including sign-resolution rules, non-reduction vs. reduction semantics, and every documented `ArithmeticException`/`NumberFormatException`/`NullPointerException` case (including the doc's own `"9999999999.5"` and `"1/0"` examples, checking the preserved `ArithmeticException` cause)
- Accessors (`getNumerator`, `getDenominator`, `getProperNumerator`, `getProperWhole`) for proper, improper, negative, and exact-whole fractions
- `Number` conversions (`doubleValue`, `floatValue`, `intValue`, `longValue`)
- `equals`/`hashCode` (including the documented 1/2 vs 2/4 inequality) and `compareTo` (including the equals-inconsistency case and `NullPointerException`)
- `abs`, `negate`, `invert` (including "not reduced" and zero-invert exception)
- `add`, `subtract`, `multiplyBy`, `divideBy` (values, null checks, divide-by-zero, and overflow via `Integer.MAX_VALUE` cases)
- `pow` (identity for power 0/1, reduction, overflow), `reduce` (simplification vs. same-instance no-op, zero-numerator case)
- `toProperString` and `toString` formatting rules

All expectations trace back to the javadoc contract in `api/`. `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`, and per instructions I did not run the tests.
